newsitem.title: USA: US WCoast late prod prices turn idle on slow trade.
newsitem.headline: US WCoast late prod prices turn idle on slow trade.

text.p: U.S. West Coast spot products prices idled late as buyers left the market and sellers rolled over their November positions into December, traders said.
"It's low retail, low racks and a desire to get out of November products," a broker said, explaining why sellers dominated the market.
Monday's fire at Texaco's Wilmington, Calif., refinery, lifted prices as much as two cents yesterday.
But traders said concerns faded quickly, amid perceptions of ample supply and Texaco's absence from spot buying.
Except for a damaged hydrotreater, the 96,000 barrel-per-day plant resumed normal operations early Tuesday, a company spokeswoman said.
She also said the company would meet customers supply needs.
After falling a half cent this morning on heavier selling, offers for conventional unleaded gasoline flattened in Los Angeles at 60.50 cents a gallon. CARB-grade offers stayed 64.50 cents.
Low sulphur diesel remained unchanged between 67 and 68 cents a gallon.
The American Petroleum Institute (API) said Tuesday it would delay the release of its weekly petroleum inventory data until Wednesday.
